title: Portable frozen byte table
summary: Attach a verified portable Engram package to inspect a frozen byte table with a trainable target adapter. This lesson requires a real package and never guesses its table size, value width, order, or dimensions.

steps.explanation: A portable scaffold copies the supplied verified package into assets/memory.engram and derives its table, value width, byte order, and final-injection settings exactly from that package.
shapes: frozen table values [B,T,M] → trainable adapter projection [B,T,D]
observe: engram lookup, reuse, gate, and norm diagnostics after attachment
first byte lookup addresses in a full probe diagnostic

steps.explanation: The package table remains frozen while its target adapter remains trainable; package widths are independent of backbone width.
shapes: package value width M is independent of model hidden width D
observe: trainability recorded by probe layer hooks

prerequisites: Supply a verified --memory-package produced by byte-engram training and engram export.
Without a package, use the complete byte-engram train → engram export → portable scaffold command sequence; no placeholder path is accepted.
try_changes: Predict which package-derived shape is independent of backbone D.
Attach one verified package, then compare only target backbone width or injection placement.
Probe trainability and verify that the package table is frozen while the adapter is trainable.
limits: No portable configuration is runnable without a verified package; dimensions are intentionally not guessed in lesson metadata.
A frozen portable table is not executable semantic memory and does not establish transfer or quality gains.

papers.title: Engram: A Neural Memory System for Language Models
papers.claim_boundary: The paper motivates memory portability questions; SparseLab only attaches verified frozen byte tables and does not reproduce the paper's broader results.
